title.narrative: The commitments under ratified ILO conventions are fulfilled and additional conventions ratified using effective consultation with social partners and other stakeholders

description.narrative:
Mongolia has revised its labour legislation in 2021 completing a process that has started a decade ago. The new legislation has extended the coverage of the law, highlighted the key labour principles including prohibition of forced labour, child labour and violence and harassment at work, started regulating new emerging labour relations etc.
Mongolia has ratified nine out of ten ILO fundamental conventions and made commitments to additionally ratify labour inspection conventions (C81 and C129), and forced labour protocol (P29) and is considering C187 on promotional framework for occupational safety and health, and C190 concerning violence and harassment.
During the current biennium, the ILO assists the Government to prepare quality reports on application of ratified conventions and its submission on time by capacitating the tripartite sub-committee on application of international labour standards, the committee established under C144 concerning tripartite consultation.
The office also supports the tripartite constituents to raise awareness of and advocate for prohibition of forced labour and child labour following the studies conducted in 2023. Forced labour training modules are developed for labour inspectors, judges, prosecutors, police officers and other law practitioners. A study on working conditions of construction workers is underway.
